transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-21
Time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan, Sofia, Mateo (Redwood); Aisha, Tom, Lena, Rajiv (Mistral Harbor)
Shared links: onboarding-runbook.pdf, security-pack.zip, pilot-dataset.csv

Summary: quick kickoff for implementation and security intake. Customer wants private VPC deployment with KMS integration, SOC 2 checklist review, and a short perf pilot to validate 99th percentile latency under 350ms for their 1k qps bursts. Discussed pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted and next steps for pilot.

[00:00] Jordan Malik: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We re-joined the room, um, quick intros from our side. I'm Jordan, AE on the account, Sofia's our CSM, and Mateo will be your SE for the pilot.
[00:12] Aisha Patel: Hi, thanks. Aisha here, I'll lead platform. Tom's infra, Lena handles security, Rajiv on product. Happy to be here.
[00:20] Sofia Chen: Great. Goal for today is to align on access, timelines, success metrics, and security asks so we can kick the pilot next week.
[00:31] Tom Erickson: Quick heads up — we run primarily in GCP in europe-west1, but we do have an air-gapped staging cluster for PHI staging, so we need clear guidance on VPC peering and private deployment options.
[00:45] Mateo Ruiz: Yeah, we can support VPC private control plane and on-prem connectors. For GCP region routing we can pin the region; performance profile for the model will change a bit based on instance type.
[00:58] Lena Ko: On security: SOC 2 is a must, plus we need KMS/HSM integration for our keys, SAML SSO, and audit logs retained for 12 months. Also curious about data residency controls and token redaction — what gets stored and for how long.
[01:15] Jordan Malik: Totally. We'll send SOC 2 and network diagram; we support KMS via customer-managed keys with our Private deployment and can integrate with common HSM providers. Audit logs and retention are configurable on Dedicated/Private.
[01:30] Rajiv Menon: For success metrics, product cares about latency more than raw throughput — our end user SLA is 300–400ms p99 for short chat flows, but batched embeddings can be slower. We'll need a pilot to see real numbers.
[01:45] Sofia Chen: Noted. Mateo, can you outline the pilot scope?
[01:50] Mateo Ruiz: Sure. Pilot plan: 48-hour perf smoke with customer sample payloads, run three traffic patterns — steady 100 rps, 1k burst spike, and long-context sessions 2k tokens. We'll test Hosted first for baseline, then move to Dedicated/private config with same model variant. We'll capture token cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates.
[02:10] Tom Erickson: Do you auto-fallback to smaller variants when capacity is saturated? That was an ask in the RFP.
[02:18] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible variants; we'll show policy config options in the runbook. There is sometimes mismatch in behaviour between hosted and private due to kernel optimizations but we can reproduce.
[02:31] Aisha Patel: Licensing question — what's the expected monthly commit for Dedicated to reach the low per-token tiers? We're trying to budget.
[02:40] Jordan Malik: We gave a starter estimate in the deck; I'll follow up with a tailored quote after we size the pilot numbers. Generally, reserved capacity at X GPUs/month gives predictable cost — we'll send the pricing sheet.
[02:52] Lena Ko: Security follow-up: how do you handle logs that might contain PII? Can we enable redaction and suppress logging of request bodies?
[03:02] Mateo Ruiz: There is prefix/KV cache and we avoid logging full request bodies by default in Private; for Hosted we have opt-in settings and tokenization-based redaction. We'll share the security-pack.zip with specifics.
[03:18] Rajiv Menon: Any blocker for us running the pilot in our project? We can open a service account and set up a VPC peering if you provide the steps.
[03:25] Sofia Chen: We'll provide an access checklist. Key items: service account with Cloud IAM roles, firewall rules for IP allowlist, and SSH access for the SE to run validation.
[03:38] Tom Erickson: Our legal team also asked for a SOC 2 plus ISO attestation. Is ISO part of your compliance pack?
[03:45] Jordan Malik: We have SOC 2 Type II; ISO 27001 is in progress for some customers — I'll confirm what artifacts we can share.
[03:53] Aisha Patel: We're looking for KMS integration with our vendor VenSafe — have you integrated with them before?
[03:58] Mateo Ruiz: We haven't done VenSafe specifically but our KMS integration layer is vendor-agnostic; expect some developer effort for vendor-specific APIs. Mateo will run a short checklist with Lena after the call.
[04:12] Lena Ko: Okay, we'll send our KMS vendor contact. Also need to validate key rotation policies.
[04:18] Jordan Malik: Action item captured.
[04:20] Speaker 1: [crosstalk] sorry just —
[04:25] Sofia Chen: No worries. On timeline — pilot to start 2025-05-26 pending access. We recommended two weeks for pilot results, but given your traffic patterns we can do 48 hours of steady-state testing plus longer soak.
[04:40] Tom Erickson: If we need on-prem later, how painful is migration from Hosted to Private?
[04:46] Mateo Ruiz: We designed the deployment abstraction to keep API the same. Model version pinning and rollouts work similarly. The heavy lift is network and key management, and kernel tuning for on-prem hardware. We can use the same prompts/evls.
[05:01] Rajiv Menon: Regarding evals: can Redwood run quality regressions between model variants so we don't see hallucination regressions when moving to quantized profiles?
[05:09] Mateo Ruiz: Yes we have a small eval harness and can run prompt set comparisons; Redwood Optimize gives quantization recommendations by workload. We'll include an example report.
[05:20] Aisha Patel: On the compliance front, our audit requires traceability of who called the model. Do you have token-level audit and RBAC?
[05:28] Jordan Malik: Yes, per-token cost traces and request-level tracing exist. RBAC via SSO/SAML and fine-grained roles are supported in Dedicated/Private.
[05:35] Elena Ko: Lena: sorry, my name is Lena. I'm curious about the observable retention — minimum? 12 months?
[05:41] Sofia Chen: Default retention is 90 days, extended retention is available as an add-on for compliance. We'll include pricing in the security pack.
[05:50] Tom Erickson: Network question — do you require IP allowlist or mutual TLS?
[05:55] Mateo Ruiz: We support mTLS for Private connections; for Hosted we recommend IP allowlist plus VPC peering for improved isolation. For GCP we'll show the peering flow.
[06:06] Rajiv Menon: Procurement — what is typical contract length for Dedicated? 12 months? 24?
[06:12] Jordan Malik: Typical is 12 or 36 month commits. We can show a 12-month reserved capacity with tiered discounts.
[06:20] Aisha Patel: Ok. Can we talk about success criteria one more time — p99 < 350ms for interactive flows and cost per 1M tokens below Y?
[06:29] Sofia Chen: We'll capture both product (latency/accuracy) and business (cost) success metrics. Pilot will provide real numbers to validate.
[06:36] Tom Erickson: Does Redwood support our internal tracing format? We use vendor X trace IDs.
[06:42] Mateo Ruiz: We can emit trace IDs and include custom headers; we'll run a quick test during pilot.
[06:48] [10:12] Jordan Malik: Quick note, some of the transcripts get messy.
[06:52] Aisha Patel: ha, yeah.
[06:55] Sofia Chen: I'll summarize action items.
[07:00] Sofia Chen: Action items recap: 1) Sofia to send onboarding runbook and access checklist (Sofia), 2) Mateo to prepare pilot config and perf plan (Mateo), 3) Jordan to send SOC 2 and pricing follow-up (Jordan), 4) Mistral to share KMS vendor details and compliance list (Lena/Aisha).
[07:18] Rajiv Menon: Sounds good. One more question — if the pilot shows we need larger memory models, what's the upgrade path?
[07:24] Mateo Ruiz: We can scale to bigger GPUs or autoscale across instance types; we'll show expected mem/cost tradeoffs in the pilot report.
[07:33] Tom Erickson: Are we going to use Redwood's embeddings for our vector DB or keep embeddings in-house?
[07:39] Jordan Malik: Either is fine; we have embedding endpoints and can provide cost/perf comparisons vs your current vendor.
[07:48] Aisha Patel: Ok, thanks all. We'll aim to open service account access by Friday.
[07:52] Sofia Chen: Great, we'll follow up with the checklist and security doc links by EOD tomorrow. Thanks everyone.
[07:58] Mateo Ruiz: Thanks — I'll slot time with Lena for KMS details.
[08:02] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and some words garbled (typical Fireflies export). References to docs are shorthand links rather than full attachments.

Recap & next steps (as spoken):
- Sofia to send onboarding-runbook.pdf and access checklist by 2025-05-22
- Jordan to send SOC 2 artifacts and pricing by 2025-05-23
- Mateo to run a 48-hour perf pilot plan and share config by 2025-05-30
- Mistral to provide KMS vendor contact and compliance list by 2025-05-23
- Schedule follow-up pricing and procurement call week of 2025-05-26

End of transcript.
